name: Vacuum polarisation measured via the Lamb shift (achievable.py:35, an entry in 'THE CENSUS OF KNOWN NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY')

source.located: No source is cited by the owner (achievable.py:35 carries the bare word MEASURED). The standard sources for the claim are: Lamb & Retherford, Phys. Rev. 72, 241 (1947) (discovery of the 2S1/2-2P1/2 splitting; no arXiv copy); Uehling, Phys. Rev. 48, 55 (1935) (the one-loop vacuum-polarisation potential; no arXiv copy); Eides, Grotch & Shelyuto, 'Theory of light hydrogenic bound states', hep-ph/0002158 (hydrogen Lamb-shift theory term by term); Antognini et al., 'Theory of the 2S-2P Lamb shift and 2S hyperfine splitting in muonic hydrogen', arXiv:1208.2637; Borie, 'Lamb shift in light muonic atoms -- revisited', arXiv:1103.1772; Jentschura, arXiv:1011.5275; Bezginov et al., Science 365, 1007 (2019) (hydrogen Lamb shift measurement); CODATA 2022, arXiv:2409.03787. For the OTHER meaning of 'vacuum polarisation' -- the renormalised <T_ab> of a quantum field in a curved background, which DOES violate energy conditions -- Visser, 'Gravitational vacuum polarization II: Energy conditions in the Boulware vacuum', gr-qc/9604008 (PRD 54, 5116 (1996)).

published_statement: NOT QUOTED FROM SOURCE (NAMED-NOT-READ; see source.via). The content the claim needs, stated here as COMPUTED rather than quoted: the one-loop QED vacuum-polarisation (Uehling) correction to the Coulomb potential shifts hydrogenic S levels by Delta E(nS) = -4 alpha (Z alpha)^4 m_r^3 c^2/(15 pi n^3 m_e^2) at leading order, i.e. -216.68 MHz (1S) and -27.08 MHz (2S) in hydrogen (computed), against a measured 2S1/2-2P1/2 interval of about +1057.8 MHz (search summary, not READ); in muonic hydrogen the same potential gives E(2P)-E(2S) = 205.0074 meV (computed), the dominant part of that Lamb shift. What any Lamb-shift experiment reads is a FREQUENCY INTERVAL between two atomic levels; the vacuum-polarisation part of it is not separately measured but is one term of the QED prediction that the measured total agrees with (in hydrogen the dominant term is the self-energy, of opposite sign).
published_hypotheses: (computed, not READ) The measured quantity is an energy-level interval of a bound atom (2S1/2-2P1/2), not an energy density and not any component of a stress tensor.

(computed, not READ) Vacuum polarisation enters that interval as a correction to the Coulomb POTENTIAL (Uehling, O(alpha)) -- it makes the potential more attractive at r < hbar/(m_e c), i.e. an effective charge Q_eff(r) >= Ze (R4); it lowers S levels.

(computed, not READ) In ordinary hydrogen the VP term is -27.08 MHz against a +1057.8 MHz total: 2.56 %, opposite in sign; the total is dominated by the electron self-energy. VP is therefore INFERRED from agreement of the full QED sum with the measured total, not isolated by the measurement. In muonic hydrogen VP is ~99 % of the 2S-2P interval, but that measurement has been used to EXTRACT the proton charge radius (search summaries, not READ), so VP enters as assumed theory there too, not as a free measured quantity.

(not READ) QED vacuum polarisation in flat space around a static charge is not the same object as 'gravitational vacuum polarisation' -- the renormalised <T_ab> of a quantum field on a curved background (Candelas; Visser gr-qc/9604008), which is the one that violates energy conditions (Boulware vacuum) and which no Lamb-shift experiment measures.
hypothesis_drift: ADDED -- achievable.py:28 heads the list 'THE CENSUS OF KNOWN NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY' and achievable.py:35 enters 'VACUUM POLARISATION  MEASURED via the Lamb shift.' Placing the item under that heading asserts that what the Lamb shift measures is a NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY. The Lamb shift measures a level interval; the VP piece of it is a strengthened Coulomb potential (Q_eff(r) >= Ze at every r, computed R4: 1.019210 at r = 1e-6/m_e falling to 1.000000 at 10/m_e), and the classical field energy density built from that effective field is positive and LARGER than the bare Coulomb one at every r checked (R4). Nothing in the measured quantity is a T_00 < 0. (Caveat, named: R4 is a statement about the effective potential the Lamb shift tests; the renormalised <T_00> of the QED vacuum around a point charge was not computed and no Lamb-shift measurement reads it.)

CONFLATED -- the negative-energy 'vacuum polarisation' of the energy-condition literature is the semiclassical curved-space one (Boulware vacuum outside a Schwarzschild horizon; Visser gr-qc/9604008 per search summary, not READ; the tree itself handles it as theory at fewster-teo-sec7-candelas-schwarzschild and bothways.py:92 'KIM & THORNE vacuum polarisation diverges at the Cauchy horizon'). achievable.py:35 attaches to that name the measurement status of the flat-space QED effect. Neither half supplies what the census line claims: the measured one is not a negative energy density, and the negative one is not measured.

STRENGTHENED -- 'MEASURED' (achievable.py:35) for a quantity that, in ordinary hydrogen, is a 2.56 % opposite-sign component of the measured total, confirmed only through agreement of the whole QED sum (computed R2). 'Tested' or 'confirmed as part of QED' is the supportable word; 'measured' would need the component to be isolated, which in hydrogen it is not.

NOT A DRIFT, recorded for balance: the tree elsewhere uses QED vacuum polarisation CORRECTLY as an atomic level shift -- limitaxis.py:300-337 (vac_pol, 'the Uehling term lowers the level, so it binds harder', anchor VP_H1S_MHZ = -217.0 MHz, reproduced here as -216.68 MHz closed form) and twoindex.py:91-95, 140 ('the single exception is vacuum polarisation' for a free ion's ionisation limit). The drift is local to the achievable.py census line and its copies.

rederivation.outcome: ALL PASS (exit 0, ~4 s; sympy for the exact radial integrals, mpmath quad for the Uehling spectral integral, CODATA 2022 constants). R1: hydrogen Uehling shift closed form -216.676 MHz (1S), -27.084 MHz (2S); the full nonrelativistic expectation value of the Uehling potential gives -214.751 / -26.844 MHz (finite-range correction 0.89 %, inside the O(Z alpha) tolerance); reproduces the tree's own anchor limitaxis.py:337 VP_H1S_MHZ = -217.0 to 0.15 %. R2: VP contributes -27.084 MHz to E(2S)-E(2P), i.e. -2.56 % of the measured +1057.8 MHz and OPPOSITE in sign. R3: muonic hydrogen Uehling E(2P)-E(2S) = 205.0074 meV (2S -219.5840, 2P -14.5766 meV), agreeing with the literature figure 205.0074 as reported by search summaries; the delta-function approximation fails by >10 % there. R4: the effective charge implied by the Uehling potential is Q_eff(r)/Ze = 1.019210, 1.015644, 1.012079, 1.008516, 1.004983, 1.001724, 1.000056, 1.000000 at r = 1e-6..10 (units hbar/m_e c) -- >= 1 everywhere, so the field the Lamb shift tests is strengthened, never reversed, and its classical energy density is positive and above the bare Coulomb value; CONTROL: a sign-flipped kernel is caught (Q_eff < Ze). What is NOT computed: the renormalised <T_00> of the QED vacuum around a point charge (no Lamb-shift experiment reads it), and the hydrogen self-energy (only its dominance is inferred from R2's 2.56 %).

lacked_data: M's hypothesis for THIS result: Lamb & Retherford (1947) and the QED theorists of 1947-1950 lacked (a) muonic hydrogen (2010), where VP is ~99 % of the 2S-2P interval rather than 2.6 %; (b) CODATA-precision alpha; (c) the proton radius as a separately constrained datum. Evidence that having them does NOT change the conclusion 'VP enters the Lamb shift as the Uehling term': the Uehling term computed here with 2022 constants reproduces 205.0074 meV for muonic hydrogen to all seven digits the later literature is reported to print, and -217 MHz for hydrogen 1S as the tree's own anchor; alpha's 2018->2022 move is 6.8e-10 and moves the VP shift by ~3e-9 relative. The one datum that DID move dramatically -- the proton radius, by ~4 % (0.8775 -> ~0.841 fm), the 'proton radius puzzle' produced by precisely this Lamb-shift measurement -- was resolved on the radius and never on vacuum polarisation (search summaries; not READ). So M's hypothesis is answered NO for the physics of the result: nothing the authors lacked changes what vacuum polarisation does to atomic levels. It is answered differently for the TREE'S USE: no amount of later data could make a Lamb-shift measurement read a negative energy density, because the measured quantity is a frequency interval and the VP it contains strengthens the Coulomb field (R4). The inaccuracy here is not in the outside art; it is in the census line's category.
grade_evidence: The result the tree names holds on a SMALLER CLASS than the tree uses it for. What stands (COMPUTED here, source NAMED-NOT-READ): vacuum polarisation is a real, quantitatively confirmed contribution to the Lamb shift -- the Uehling term is -27.08 MHz (H 2S), -216.68 MHz (H 1S, the tree's own limitaxis.py anchor reproduced) and 205.0074 meV (muonic H 2P-2S), all reproduced in rederive/lamb-shift-vacuum-polarisation.py. What the tree adds (achievable.py:28, 35): that this is a MEASURED instance of NEGATIVE ENERGY DENSITY. Computed against it: the Lamb shift reads a frequency interval; the VP component is a strengthened Coulomb potential (Q_eff(r) >= Ze at every r, R4), whose classical field energy density is positive and larger than the bare one; in ordinary hydrogen VP is a -2.56 % opposite-sign component inferred from agreement of the whole QED sum, not isolated (R2). The energy-condition-violating 'vacuum polarisation' of the literature is the semiclassical curved-space one (Visser gr-qc/9604008, Boulware vacuum -- NAMED-NOT-READ, search summary), which is theory and unmeasured. So the census line merges a measured effect that is not a negative energy density with a negative energy density that is not measured. Not WRONG: nothing here computes the renormalised QED <T_00> around a charge, so no contradiction with 'vacuum polarisation has negative energy density somewhere' is SHOWN -- only that the Lamb shift does not measure one. Not OPEN: the narrowing does not depend on the unread sources' wording; it follows from what a Lamb-shift experiment observes and from the computed sign of the Uehling correction. Effect on the tree's verdict, stated both ways: removing or re-labelling this census entry does NOT weaken achievable.py's SURVEY refusal (a census of sources that do not suffice loses an item that was never a usable source), and it does NOT open a door for M either (flat-space QED VP supplies no negative T_00 to a core). The 'MEASURED' half is itself unread at source this stage; that caveat is part of the grade.
what_would_change_the_grade: (1) To STANDS: a source READ at alphaXiv showing that a Lamb-shift measurement (or any atomic-spectroscopy measurement) isolates a negative renormalised energy density of the QED vacuum -- none is known to this auditor, and R4 shows the tested potential strengthens the field. Or the owner re-scoping the line to 'vacuum polarisation: a measured LEVEL SHIFT (Lamb shift); its negative-energy form is the curved-space semiclassical one, theory, unmeasured' -- which would make it STAND as used. (2) To OPEN: if a reviewer rules that a NAMED-NOT-READ source forbids any grade above OPEN regardless of computation (the sibling fewster-teo-sec7-candelas-schwarzschild audit took that route when nothing was computable); here the narrowing is computed, so NARROWED is kept, but re-running the read when the alphaXiv quota resets is required before the report is quoted: answer_pdf_queries on 1208.2637 (Uehling 205.0074 meV, table item), hep-ph/0002158 (Uehling -4 alpha(Z alpha)^4 m/(15 pi n^3), H Lamb-shift budget), gr-qc/9604008 (abstract, energy conditions in Boulware vacuum). (3) To WRONG: a computation of the renormalised QED <T_00> around a point charge showing it is non-negative everywhere, which would contradict any reading of the line -- not attempted here.
